title: Serving the Weak
definition: Serving the Weak is Christlike care for those who are vulnerable, burdened, overlooked, or in need of help.
summary: Serving the Weak is Christlike care for those who are vulnerable, burdened, overlooked, or in need of help.
christFocus: Jesus moves toward the weak with compassion, bears burdens, and teaches His people to honor those the world often overlooks.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture calls believers to move toward weakness rather than despise it. The Church should care for the vulnerable, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and bear burdens.

Serving the weak reflects the heart of Christ, who did not build His ministry around the impressive but welcomed the weary, sick, poor, outcast, and broken.

This service is not pity from above. It is family love within the body of Christ, where every member has dignity and value.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people with disabilities, wounds, or hardships have been treated as burdens instead of gifts. Serving the weak shows that Christ’s body honors those the world may ignore.

This doctrine also confronts selfish strength. Strength is given for service, not superiority.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look for someone who needs support, dignity, or encouragement. Serve practically, listen patiently, and ask the Holy Spirit to make Christ’s compassion visible through you.
